# Original page-border controls

These are original, manually authored OOXML packages, generated by
`tools/page_borders_fixture.py`, `tools/page_border_stories_fixture.py` and
`tools/page_border_sides_fixture.py`. They reuse only the original cell-end-context
package skeleton; no third-party template or rendering implementation is included.

The reference application exported the retained PDFs with `tools/export-reference.ps1`.
`tools/record_page_borders.py` records SHA-256 provenance, page-edge ink bounds,
corner pixels and overlap colors from those PDFs at four pixels per point.

- `control`: 24 pages, twelve two-page sections, page/text origin, three display
  modes and front/back ordering. First-page display restarts at each section.
- `overlap`: three pages, paragraph shading intersects the frame, proving front,
  back and omitted (front) ordering.
- `stories`, `exclude-header`, `exclude-footer`, `exclude-both`: eight pages,
  text-relative frames include the header/footer distances unless excluded.
- `widths`: eight pages, omitted/0/1/2/4/8/96/200 eighth-point sizes. The reference application paints
  ordinary lines on a 600-dpi grid with a 0.12-point minimum, retaining large
  authored widths. Bounds use a 0.3-point raster comparison tolerance.
- `sides`: six pages, each independent side, top/right, and unequal widths/spaces.

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.6.10 describes pgBorders and the shared CT_Border
attributes describe eighth-point widths and point spacing. Native controls record
the reference application's width quantization and header/footer treatment. The width specification
permits reassignment outside 2..96; the reference application's retained large values are observed
behavior, not proof of a mandatory-spec violation.

The native comparisons here verify single-line frames. Other recognized line
patterns reuse paragraph-border painting; their page-corner fidelity is not fully
verified. Artwork and visible shadows remain guarded as unsupported. Continuous
sections sharing a page, even/odd filler pages and alignBordersAndEdges combinations
need further native coverage. These limits are not completion claims.
